image_description: A single, dark grey or black bookshelf-style loudspeaker standing on a carpeted floor against a light wall. The speaker has a rectangular enclosure with rounded vertical edges. It features two visible circular drivers: a smaller top driver (tweeter/mid-range) and a larger bottom driver (woofer). There is a control panel with small blue illuminated buttons or indicators at the very bottom front. A black power cable extends from the rear right side.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object clearly exhibits a rectangular, box-like structure typical of bookshelf speakers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: One or more circular speaker cones on front face of varying sizes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct circular drivers are visible on the front face, one significantly larger than the other.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The lower driver is larger (woofer) and the upper driver is smaller (tweeter), arranged vertically as described.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cone surface made of paper, polypropylene, or composite with rubber surround.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The drivers show characteristic concentric rings and a central dust cap, consistent with standard speaker cone construction materials.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Grille cloth or perforated metal may cover the drivers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The drivers are exposed; there is no grille cloth or perforated metal covering them.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Terminal connections visible on rear panel.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the front and slight side view; the rear panel is completely occluded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wood, MDF, or plastic enclosure with black, white, or wood-grain finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The enclosure has a smooth, matte dark finish consistent with painted MDF or plastic.
The visual features (drivers, enclosure shape) definitively identify it as an electro-acoustic transducer.
Contextual cues (power cable, control buttons) support its function as an active audio output device.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The blue illuminated squares/buttons at the bottom lack clear, legible symbols or text. They appear as generic glowing rectangles rather than functional icons, which is a common AI artifact in rendering small UI elements.
The rubber surrounds of the drivers appear slightly overly smooth and uniform, lacking the fine micro-texture often seen in real rubber components, though this could also be due to image resolution.
The top edge of the speaker cabinet appears slightly warped or uneven rather than perfectly straight, suggesting minor geometric instability in the generation.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of speaker (e.g., active bookshelf monitor) and verify class conformance against ImageNet taxonomy.
To verify the 3D structural integrity of the box shape and ensure the drivers are correctly recessed/flush with the baffle.
To check for clean boundaries between the driver cones, surrounds, and the main enclosure, ensuring no fusion or bleeding artifacts.
To specifically analyze the low-severity text/symbol gibberish on the bottom interface and overall texture realism.

focus_areas: Structural geometry of the enclosure (straight lines, correct perspective)
Anatomical correctness of speaker drivers (concentricity, surround texture)
Legibility and logic of the control interface buttons
Boundary sharpness between drivers and cabinet
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the control panel at the bottom. AI models often struggle with small, detailed UI elements, resulting in 'gibberish' lights or buttons. Also, verify if the perspective lines of the cabinet are truly straight or if there is subtle warping. Check if the driver cones look physically plausible (correct depth/recession).
